changes.pattern: Reader-only teams sometimes end with multiple answer lines, list both compared entities, or stop before a clean final answer.
changes.rationale: In reader-only traces the final output is not a single extracted span: A2 wrote both the entity and the compared year and the final answer became the year, A93 listed both entities when only one satisfied the condition, A84 was cut before a clean yes/no answer, and A53/A122 gave a shortened name instead of the name form needed. The reader role currently only says 'give a short answer', so the 9B model is not forced to terminate with one direct answer span. Editing the reader self-harness is the right layer because these failures occur in the final reader node and the practice applies to every reader-only question.

ops.name: reader
ops.role: You answer multi-hop questions using only the given paragraphs: find each fact you need and give a short answer. End with exactly one line starting with #### followed by only the answer span that directly answers the question.

changes.pattern: Checker nodes often rubber-stamp the input answer instead of replacing it with the exact span from the supporting paragraph sentence.
changes.rationale: In many traced bridge failures the decomposer found the right entity or fact but gave a wrong span form, and the checker said the input was correct and repeated it: A3 kept 'the Bahamian island of Great Exuma' instead of 'Great Exuma', A44 and A76 kept the extra 'County', A107 kept the unit, A18 kept the extra code-number phrase, and A4/A58/A137/A144/A146 kept shortened person names instead of the name form in the supporting sentence. The current checker role says 'verify each hop, fix any error' but does not tell the model to compare the input answer to the exact supporting span or to replace it when they differ. Editing the checker role is the right layer because the checker is the final node in most bridge teams and can correct span-form errors without changing the decomposer's search behavior.

ops.name: checker
ops.role: You check the answers you are given against the paragraphs: verify each hop, fix any error, and give the short answer you believe is correct. If no input is given, answer the question directly. Do not repeat an input answer unless the supporting sentence contains that exact span; otherwise replace it with the span from the supporting sentence that directly answers the question. End with exactly one line starting with #### followed by only the answer.

changes.pattern: Comparison and yes/no questions are sometimes staffed with unnecessary decomposer/checker teams or without the high-value comparison/yes_no and date tools, causing wrong entities, both entities, dates instead of entities, or checker changes from correct to wrong.
changes.rationale: Traces such as A36 show an inputless checker changing a correct comparison answer, A93 lists both entities instead of the one satisfying the condition, A2 outputs the compared year instead of the entity, and A42/A53/A122 involve date comparison. The residual table shows comparison and dates are strongly associated with correct answers when given. A specific rule for this question class can improve staffing without changing bridge behavior.

ops.text: Comparison or yes/no question: use exactly one reader and return it. Give the reader search and the matching skill (comparison or yes_no); add dates when the compared property is a year, date, age, or order.

changes.pattern: The meta-agent over-applies the harmful distractors skill to ordinary bridge and comparison questions, and under-applies the high-value dates tool to date-sensitive questions.
changes.rationale: The residual-harness table shows distractors lowers node accuracy when given, while dates is one of the strongest tools. Rule 3 is currently too vague, so the 9B meta-agent attaches distractors broadly and misses dates. This change keeps the rule short and targets only equipment choices, avoiding the broader skill-assignment edits that regressed previously.

ops.text: Give skills that match the question. Give the dates tool when the question depends on years, dates, ages, order, or overlap. Give distractors only when the same or very similar name appears in multiple paragraphs.

changes.pattern: Comparison and yes/no nodes often miss the question-type skill or answer_span, so they output dates, both entities, or non-answers instead of the required entity or yes/no.
changes.rationale: Rule 1 only says to use one reader and does not equip it. Traces A21, A22, A84, and A122 show reader nodes without comparison/yes_no plus answer_span, and A2/A93 show comparison nodes still outputting the compared value or both entities. Putting the skill requirement in the comparison/yes/no staffing rule makes the residual harness consistent for this question class.

ops.text: Comparison or yes/no question: one reader with the matching question-type skill (comparison or yes_no) plus answer_span.

changes.pattern: Final answers are not verbatim spans: names are shortened, descriptors are added, or the compared value is returned instead of the requested entity.
changes.rationale: Many wrong traces have the correct fact found but the final line altered: A3, A44, A107, A137, A144, and A146 add or drop words; A2 and A93 return a value or both entities. The current answer_span skill says 'shortest span', which encourages dropping middle names or needed qualifiers. Replacing it with a verbatim-span instruction targets the final-answer step without changing architecture.

ops.name: answer_span
ops.text: Give the exact span from the paragraphs that directly answers the question. Copy it verbatim: do not paraphrase, add explanations, or change a source name to a shorter or longer form.

changes.pattern: The comparison skill tells the agent to answer with the entity's name as written in the question, which preserves short question forms instead of the fuller paragraph form.
changes.rationale: In A21, A53, and A122 the question names people by short forms, but the correct answers are the fuller names from their own paragraphs. The current comparison skill explicitly says 'as written in the question', which directly causes this. Editing the skill fixes the question-class instruction where the failure originates.

ops.name: comparison
ops.when: two entities are compared (which / who is older, earlier, larger; do both ...; same ...)
ops.text: 1. Find the compared property for each entity in its own paragraph; write both values. 2. Compare them carefully (earlier date = older person / earlier release). 3. Answer with the single entity that satisfies the question, using the name form from the paragraphs, not the shorter form from the question. For 'both' and 'same' questions, answer yes/no.

changes.pattern: The distractors skill is over-applied to ordinary related-entity questions and can steer agents toward ignoring useful paragraphs or producing distractor-focused output.
changes.rationale: The residual table shows distractors is the only skill that lowers node accuracy (50% when given vs 60% otherwise), and traces such as A132 and A127 show distractor-focused reasoning or wrong entity selection when the skill is attached. Narrowing the skill's stated trigger reduces over-application without removing the capability for true same-name/similar-name cases.

ops.name: distractors
ops.when: similar names or several entities with the same name, not merely related entities
ops.text: Confirm the exact entity by its title and description before using a fact from its paragraph. Ignore facts from paragraphs about a different entity that has a similar or identical name.
